change_interpretations.engineering_summary: The allowed transient spike duration to be ignored is reduced from 10 ms to 5 ms, requiring the controller to filter out shorter spikes more aggressively.

assessments.reason: The test validates torque response time (VCU-DR-01) and does not involve pedal‑signal spike filtering, which is the only changed behaviour.
evidence: procedure checks torque within 100 ms after pedal validation

assessments.reason: The test covers arbitration between brake and pedal (VCU-DR-01, VCU-BRK-03) and does not exercise the spike‑filter limit that changed.
The test measures high‑load torque transient timing (92 ms) and has no reference to pedal‑signal spikes or VCU-DR-02.
evidence: procedure sweeps demand 75–95 % and records 92 ms

assessments.reason: The test validates emergency‑brake command latency (VCU-BRK-03) and does not involve the spike‑filter requirement.
evidence: procedure targets brake command latency within 100 ms

assessments.reason: The test checks wheel‑speed sensor failure handling (VCU-DGN-04) and is unrelated to pedal‑signal spike filtering.
evidence: procedure unplug wheel‑speed sensor and verify degraded mode

assessments.reason: The test records mode‑change audit data (VCU-LOG-05) and does not address the changed spike‑filter requirement.
evidence: procedure change Comfort to Sport and log timestamp

assessments.reason: The test has a TBD requirement link and exercises thermal‑load acceleration; it does not inject or evaluate pedal spikes.
evidence: procedure uses 80 % pedal, no spike injection

assessments.reason: The test replays an old diagnostic trace (unknown requirement) and does not involve pedal‑signal spike handling.
The test compares torque ramps between modes (VCU-MOD-06) and contains no spike‑filter verification.
evidence: procedure compares Sport vs Comfort response

assessments.reason: The test injects a 7 ms pedal pulse to verify that no torque is generated; the new limit (5 ms) means a 7 ms spike should no longer be ignored, so the existing PASS evidence is no longer valid.
evidence: procedure inject 7 ms false pedal pulse
old limit 10 ms, new limit 5 ms
assessments.recommended_action: Revise the procedure to use a pulse ≤5 ms (e.g., 3 ms) and rerun the test to obtain evidence against the tightened requirement.

assessments.reason: The test validates brake‑override priority (VCU-BRK-03) and does not involve pedal‑signal spike filtering.
evidence: procedure requests emergency braking while torque demand is high

assessments.reason: The test measures ECU wake‑up time (no linked requirement) and is unrelated to the spike‑filter change.
evidence: procedure power cycles ECU and checks readiness within 500 ms
